nahhas-irab:31-31.t: (وَما أَنْتُمْ بِمُعْجِزِينَ): Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: that is, "[you are not] outrunning [Him]". One says أعجز when someone runs and outstrips.

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: «الجواري» is the plural of جارية; الجواري is in the position of the nominative (rafʿ); the ḍamma was dropped from its yāʾ because of its heaviness.

nahhas-irab:33-35.t:
(إِنْ يَشَأْ يُسْكِنِ الرِّيحَ): a condition and its requital (sharṭ wa-mujāzāh). (فَيَظْلَلْنَ) is conjoined (maʿṭūf), and likewise (أَوْ يُوبِقْهُنَّ), and likewise (وَيَعْفُ), and likewise, according to Sībawayh, (وَيَعْلَمَ الَّذِينَ يُجادِلُونَ فِي آياتِنا): this is the preferred choice in his view, because it is speech conjoined part upon part. Similar to it is يُحاسِبْكُمْ بِهِ اللَّهُ فَيَغْفِرُ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ وَيُعَذِّبُ مَنْ يَشاءُ [al-Baqara: 284], and likewise the saying of al-Nābigha [metre: al-wāfir], verse 401:
فإن يهلك أبو قابوس يهلك ... ربيع النّاس والبلد الحرام
ونمسك بعده بذناب عيس ... أجبّ الظّهر ليس له سنام
(If Abū Qābūs perishes, the spring of the people and the sacred land perish; and after him we shall cling to the tail of a life whose back is cut, having no hump.)
So he put «ونمسك» in the jussive (jazm) by conjunction. Its nominative and accusative are also permissible, except that the nominative is better in Sībawayh's view, and it is the reading of the Medinans: (وَيَعْلَمَ الَّذِينَ) [Translator's note: so vowelled in the source, though the nominative reading (وَيَعْلَمُ) is what is meant here], taking it as cut off from what precedes it and nominative. The accusative is far-fetched in his view, and it is the reading of the Kufans and the sound transmission of the reading of Abū ʿAmr. Sībawayh likened it, in its far-fetchedness, to the saying of the poet [metre: al-wāfir], verse 402:
سأترك منزلي لبني تميم ... وألحق بالحجاز فأستريحا
(I shall leave my dwelling to Banū Tamīm and join the Ḥijāz, and so find rest.)
Except that the accusative in the verse [of the Quran] is more fitting, because it is a condition, and that is not something affirmed. And he recited [metre: al-ṭawīl], verse 403:
ومن يغترب عن قومه لا يزل يرى ... مصارع أقوام مجرّا ومسحبا
وتدفن منه الصّالحات وإن يسيء ... يكن ما أساء النّار في رأس كبكبا
(Whoever goes abroad from his people will keep seeing the death-places of peoples, dragged and hauled; his good deeds are buried, and if he does wrong, what he did wrong becomes a fire on the top of Kabkab.)
So he put «وتدفن» in the accusative, though had he put it in the nominative it would have been better. Abū ʿUbayd chose the accusative and likened it to His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: وَلَمَّا يَعْلَمِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ جاهَدُوا مِنْكُمْ وَيَعْلَمَ الصَّابِرِينَ [Āl ʿImrān: 142].
But the two are not of the same kind and do not resemble each other, because «ويعلم» there is a response to something containing negation, so the accusative is more appropriate for it, whereas His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He, (وَيَعْلَمَ الَّذِينَ يُجادِلُونَ) is not a response such that its accusative would be required. The position of الذين in His saying «ويعلم النّاس» [Translator's note: so in the source; «ويعلم الذين» is apparently meant] is the position of the nominative, by (يعلم).

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: (وَما عِنْدَ اللَّهِ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (خَيْرٌ) is its khabar (predicate); (وَأَبْقى) is conjoined to خير; (لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا) is genitive (khafḍ) by the lām.

nahhas-irab:37-37.t:
(وَالَّذِينَ) is in the position of the genitive (khafḍ), conjoined to «للذين آمنوا». (يَجْتَنِبُونَ كَبائِرَ الْإِثْمِ): this is the reading of the Medinans, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim; Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read it as كَبائِرَ الْإِثْمِ» [Translator's note: so in the source; from what follows, the reading of this second group is «كبير الإثم» in the singular].
The first reading is clearer, because if one reads كبير it gives the impression that it is a single one, the greatest of them, and the meaning is not that according to any of the exegetes, except for something al-Farrāʾ said, in which he reversed the view of the exegetes. He said: «كبير الإثم» is shirk (associating partners with Allah); and he said: كبائر may be used to mean كبير. This is reversed; rather one says: كبير is used to mean كبائر, being a singular that indicates a plural. He also claimed that it is recommended for whoever reads «كبائر الإثم» to read «والفواحش» in the genitive; but reading thus contradicts the proof of consensus. And stranger than this is that he claimed that reading it thus is recommended, and then said: "I have not heard anyone read it so."
The ḥadīths from the Prophet ﷺ about the major sins (al-kabāʾir) are well known and numerous, and [likewise] from the Companions and the Successors. We shall mention of them what suffices to make this clear, and we shall explain the meaning of al-kabāʾir and the disagreement about it, since it is something no one may be ignorant of. We begin with what is authentic about it from the Messenger ﷺ, whose chain of transmission (isnād) is unimpeachable, and follow it with sayings of the Companions, the Successors and the people of reasoning, with what suffices, if Allah wills.
Among that is what Muḥammad ibn Idrīs ibn Aswad narrated to us from Ibrāhīm ibn Marzūq, who said: Wahb ibn Jarīr narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Bakr ibn Anas, from Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: «The greatest of the major sins are associating partners with Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, disobedience to Muslim parents, killing a soul, and false testimony (or: false speech).»
And it was read before Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb [al-Nasāʾī], from ʿAbda ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥīm, who said: Ibn Shumayl informed us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, he said: Firās narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Shaʿbī narrating from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: «The major sins are associating partners with Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, disobedience to parents, killing a soul, and the engulfing oath (al-yamīn al-ghamūs).»
Aḥmad said: Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm informed us: Baqiyya narrated to us: Baḥīr ibn Saʿd narrated to me, from Khālid ibn Maʿdān [Translator's note: the source has «معد»], that Abū Ruhm al-Samāʿī narrated to him from Abū Ayyūb — he is Khālid ibn Zayd al-Anṣārī, a veteran of Badr and of al-ʿAqaba — from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: «Whoever comes not associating anything with Allah, establishing the prayer, giving the zakāt, fasting Ramaḍān and avoiding the major sins, he is in Paradise.» The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about the major sins, and he said: «Associating partners with Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, killing a Muslim soul, and fleeing on the day of the advance [in battle].»
Aḥmad said: ʿAmr ibn ʿAlī informed us, he said: Yaḥyā narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash and Manṣūr, from Abū Wāʾil, from Abū Maysara, from ʿAbd Allāh, who said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, which sin is greatest?" He said: «That you set up a rival to Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, when He created you.» I said: "Then which?" He said: «That you kill your child for fear that it will eat with you.» I said: "Then which?" He said: «That you commit adultery with your neighbour's wife.»
Abū Jaʿfar said: These are sound chains of transmission. In the ḥadīth of Abū Umāma there is an addition to the major sins in them; in it are: consuming the orphan's property, slandering a chaste woman, misappropriating spoils (al-ghulūl), sorcery and consuming usury. This is all that we know to have been narrated from the Prophet ﷺ about the major sins in detail and explicitly. As for the summary ḥadīth, namely what Abū Saʿīd and Abū Hurayra narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that they are seven, it does not contradict this, because slandering a chaste woman, the engulfing oath and sorcery fall under false speech, and the ḥadīth of Ibn Masʿūd in which is «that you kill your child for fear that it will eat with you» falls under killing the forbidden soul. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not say: "The major sins are only these," such that submission [to that limit] would be required.
Masrūq narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd that he said: The major sins are from the beginning of Sūrat al-Nisāʾ up to the head of the thirtieth verse: إِنْ تَجْتَنِبُوا كَبائِرَ ما تُنْهَوْنَ عَنْهُ نُكَفِّرْ عَنْكُمْ سَيِّئاتِكُمْ [al-Nisāʾ: 31].
The most fitting and most comprehensive of what has been said about the major sins is what ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, he said: al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad al-Zaʿfarānī said: Abū Qaṭan narrated to us, from Yazīd ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās was asked about the major sins and said: "Everything that Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, has forbidden is among the major sins," until he mentioned the glance (al-ṭarfa). And Bakr ibn Sahl narrated it to us, he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, from Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "The major sins are everything that Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, has sealed with Fire, wrath, a curse or punishment."
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a good, clear statement, because Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: إِنْ تَجْتَنِبُوا كَبائِرَ ما تُنْهَوْنَ عَنْهُ نُكَفِّرْ عَنْكُمْ سَيِّئاتِكُمْ [al-Nisāʾ: 31], so it is understood from this that one who avoids the major sins is not punished for the minor sins. So when Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, has made known that He brings [a person] into the Fire for a sin, it is known that it is a major sin; and likewise when He has commanded that its doer be punished in this world with a prescribed penalty (ḥadd). Likewise al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: "Every binding [sin] for whose people Allah the Exalted has made punishment binding is a major sin, and everything for which a ḥadd is established is a major sin." This meaning that we have explained after mentioning the ḥadīths with chains is also an explanation of the saying of Allah the Exalted: إِنْ تَجْتَنِبُوا كَبائِرَ ما تُنْهَوْنَ عَنْهُ, and of all that is like it.

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: (وَالَّذِينَ اسْتَجابُوا لِرَبِّهِمْ) is in the position of the genitive (khafḍ); the meaning is: "and what is with Allah is better and more lasting for those who believe and for those who respond to their Lord". (وَأَقامُوا الصَّلاةَ): that is, they perform it completely with its limits: its bowing, its prostration and its humility. (وَأَمْرُهُمْ شُورى بَيْنَهُمْ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:39-39.t: (وَالَّذِينَ إِذا أَصابَهُمُ الْبَغْيُ) is in the position of the genitive, like the first. (هُمْ يَنْتَصِرُونَ): this is praise of them; they are described as not surrendering when a transgressor transgresses against them or a wrongdoer wrongs them, because if they surrendered to him they would not be forbidding what is wrong, and his doing that to them is a wrong. In the ḥadīth of Ḥudhayfa from the Prophet ﷺ: «It is not lawful for a Muslim to abase himself.» It was said: "How does he abase himself?" He said: «He takes upon himself trials he cannot bear.»

nahhas-irab:40-40.t: (وَجَزاءُ سَيِّئَةٍ سَيِّئَةٌ مِثْلُها): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). The first «سيّئة» is an evil deed in the literal sense, and the second figuratively; it is called «سيّئة» because it is a requital for the first, so that it be known that retaliation is taken with the like of what was inflicted on him. (فَمَنْ عَفا وَأَصْلَحَ فَأَجْرُهُ عَلَى اللَّهِ): that is, he did not take retaliation, so his reward is upon Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, as al-Ḥasan, Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir, ʿAṭāʾ and Muḥammad narrated, saying that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «A caller will call on the Day of Resurrection: "Where is the one who has a promise upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He? Let him stand." And the one who pardoned will stand.» And ʿAṭāʾ recited: فَمَنْ عَفا وَأَصْلَحَ فَأَجْرُهُ عَلَى اللَّهِ.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: (وَلَمَنِ انْتَصَرَ بَعْدَ ظُلْمِهِ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (فَأُولئِكَ) is also a mubtadaʾ, and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the first.

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: (إِنَّمَا السَّبِيلُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ يَظْلِمُونَ النَّاسَ): that is, the way of punishment.

nahhas-irab:43-43.t:
That is, among the loftiest and most exalted of [matters] is that one pardon and overlook, and guard against doubtful matters even if they are not forbidden, out of scrupulousness and seeking the good pleasure of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. These are the lofty matters, and they are among (عزم الأمور), that is, the [matters] on which the scrupulous and God-fearing resolve.
Abū Jaʿfar said: There is a difficulty here from the standpoint of Arabic, namely that «لمن صبر وغفر» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and it has no khabar (predicate) in the wording. What is said about it is that there is an omission in it, the implied form being: "and as for one who is patient and pardons, that [on his part] is among the matters of resolve". The like of this is plentiful and found in the speech of the Arabs; Sībawayh and others reported it: «مررت ببرّ قفيز بدرهم» ("I passed by wheat, a qafīz for a dirham"), that is, "a qafīz of it"; and one says: «السّمن منوان بدرهم» ("ghee, two manns for a dirham"), meaning "of it".

nahhas-irab:44-44.t:
(وَمَنْ يُضْلِلِ اللَّهُ فَما لَهُ مِنْ وَلِيٍّ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ): that is, whomever He leads astray from the reward has no protector and no helper to ask the reward for him. (وَتَرَى الظَّالِمِينَ لَمَّا رَأَوُا الْعَذابَ يَقُولُونَ) is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(هَلْ إِلى مَرَدٍّ مِنْ سَبِيلٍ): «من» is redundant (zāʾida), for emphasis.

nahhas-irab:45-45.t: (وَتَراهُمْ يُعْرَضُونَ عَلَيْها خاشِعِينَ): [accusative] as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and likewise (يَنْظُرُونَ مِنْ طَرْفٍ خَفِيٍّ). Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb said: they steal glances at the Fire. (وَقالَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنَّ الْخاسِرِينَ الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ وَأَهْلِيهِمْ): ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: They are those who were created for the Fire and the Fire was created for them; they left their wealth and their families behind in this world, were deprived of Paradise and went to the Fire, so they lost this world and the Hereafter.

nahhas-irab:46-46.t: (مِنْ أَوْلِياءَ) is in the position of the nominative, as the noun (ism) of kāna.

nahhas-irab:47-47.t: (ما لَكُمْ مِنْ مَلْجَإٍ يَوْمَئِذٍ وَما لَكُمْ مِنْ نَكِيرٍ): that is, [you have] no escape, and you will not deny what you have been made to stand upon of your deeds.

nahhas-irab:48-49.t:
(وَإِنَّا إِذا أَذَقْنَا الْإِنْسانَ مِنَّا رَحْمَةً), then He said afterwards (وَإِنْ تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ), so the pronoun came [as the pronoun] of a group, because الإنسان is a generic noun meaning "all", as He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: إِنَّ الْإِنْسانَ لَفِي خُسْرٍ إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا [al-ʿAṣr: 2–3]; the exception occurred because الإنسان means a plural.
(يَهَبُ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ إِناثاً وَيَهَبُ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ الذُّكُورَ): that is, of children.

nahhas-irab:50-50.t: (أَوْ يُزَوِّجُهُمْ ذُكْراناً وَإِناثاً): that is, He combines this for them; as Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyya said: he means by it twins. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: يزوّجهم means "He pairs [them] for them"; and any two that are paired are a زوجان (pair). (وَيَجْعَلُ مَنْ يَشاءُ عَقِيماً): that is, no child is born to him. عقيم has the meaning of معقوم (passive). One says عقمت المرأة when the woman does not conceive; she is then امرأة عقيم and معقومة (a barren woman).

nahhas-irab:51-51.t:
(أَنْ) is in the position of the nominative, as the noun (ism) of kāna. (وَحْياً) may be a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), as you say: جاء فلان مشيا ("So-and-so came walking"); and it may be accusative as a maṣdar. (أَوْ مِنْ وَراءِ حِجابٍ أَوْ يُرْسِلَ رَسُولًا فَيُوحِيَ بِإِذْنِهِ ما يَشاءُ): this is the reading of most people. Nāfiʿ read (أَوْ يُرْسِلَ رَسُولًا) [Translator's note: so vowelled in the source] in the nominative, and (فَيُوحِيَ) with the yāʾ made quiescent [i.e. أو يرسلُ … فيوحي]. We do not know it to be narrated from anyone but Nāfiʿ, except that he said: "I have not read a single word on which two of the imams did not agree"; for this reason ʿAbd Allāh ibn Wahb said: "The reading of Nāfiʿ is sunna."
Abū Jaʿfar said: As for the discussion of the accusative of «يرسل» and «يوحي» and their nominative, Sībawayh brought it from al-Khalīl with what suffices for whoever reflects on it, and we dictate it verbatim as he said it, so that it be more satisfying. Sībawayh said: I asked al-Khalīl about the saying of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He: أَوْ يُرْسِلَ رَسُولًا فَيُوحِيَ بِإِذْنِهِ ما يَشاءُ, and he held that the accusative is construed on an «أن» other than this one; had this word been [construed] on this «أن», the speech would have had no valid sense. But when He said إِلَّا وَحْياً, it was in the meaning of "except that He reveals", and «أو يرسل» was a verb that cannot run on «إلّا», so it was made to run on this [other] «أن», as though He said: "except that He reveals or sends", because had He said "except by revelation and except that He sends" it would have been good, and «أن يرسل» would be in the standing of «الإرسال» (sending, a maṣdar). So they construed it on «أن», since it was not permissible for them to say "or except He sends"; so it is as though He said: "except by revelation or that He sends".
And al-Ḥuṣayn ibn al-Ḥumām al-Murrī said [metre: al-ṭawīl], verse 404:
ولولا رجال من رزام أعزّة ... وآل سبيع أو أسوءك علقما
(Were it not for mighty men of Rizām, and the family of Subayʿ, or [were it not] that I would grieve you, ʿAlqama…)
He implies «أن»; that is because it was impossible to make the verb run on لولا, so he implied «أن», as though he said: "were it not for that, or were it not that I would grieve you".
And it reached us that the people of Medina put this verse in the nominative: وَما كانَ لِبَشَرٍ أَنْ يُكَلِّمَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَّا وَحْياً أَوْ مِنْ وَراءِ حِجابٍ أَوْ يُرْسِلَ رَسُولًا فَيُوحِيَ بِإِذْنِهِ [Translator's note: so vowelled in the source, though the nominative is what is being discussed]. So it is as though — and Allah knows best — He said: Allah does not speak to human beings except by revelation, or He sends a messenger, that is, in this state; and this is His speaking to them, as the Arabs say: "Your greeting is the blow, your reproach is the sword, and your speech is killing." ʿAmr ibn Maʿdī Karib said [metre: al-wāfir], verse 405:
وخيل قد دلفت لها بخيل ... تحيّة بينهم ضرب وجيع
(Many a cavalry I advanced against with cavalry; the greeting between them was a painful blow.)
And I asked al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him, about the saying of al-Aʿshā [metre: al-basīṭ], verse 406:
إن تركبوا فركوب الخيل عادتنا ... أو تنزلون فإنا معشر نزل
(If you ride, then riding horses is our custom; or [if] you dismount, then we are a people who dismount [to fight].)
He said: the speech here is on [the pattern of] your saying "it will be thus or it will be thus"; [since] its position, had he said in it "Will you ride?", the meaning would not be spoiled, it became in the standing of «ولا سابق شيئا» [Translator's note: the wording of this passage is compressed in the source and is translated as written]. As for Yūnus, he said: I put it in the nominative as a new start (ibtidāʾ), as though he said: "or you are dismounting". On this approach the nominative in the verse is explained, as though He said: "or He sends a messenger", as Ṭarafa said [metre: al-ṭawīl], verse 407:
أو أنا مفتدى
("…or I am ransomed")
And the view of Yūnus is easier.

nahhas-irab:52-52.t: (وَكَذلِكَ أَوْحَيْنا إِلَيْكَ رُوحاً مِنْ أَمْرِنا): the kāf is in the position of the accusative, that is: We revealed to you a revelation like that which We have related to you. (ما كُنْتَ تَدْرِي مَا الْكِتابُ وَلَا الْإِيمانُ): «ما» is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «الكتاب» is its khabar (predicate), and the clause is in the position of the accusative by تدري. It is permissible in ordinary speech to put الكتاب in the accusative and make «ما» redundant (zāʾida), as was narrated: هذا «باب علم ما الكلم من العربية» ("This is the chapter on knowing what words are in Arabic"), where «الكلم» was put in the accusative. (وَلكِنْ جَعَلْناهُ نُوراً): He did not say «جعلناهما» (We made them both), so the pronoun refers to the Book, or to the revelation, or to faith. The more fitting of the two is that it refers to the Book, with faith conjoined to it, and so it is without omission. (وَإِنَّكَ لَتَهْدِي إِلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ): al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: الصراط is the path and guidance. And it is read وَإِنَّكَ لَتَهْدِي [Translator's note: so in the source, identical to the reading just given; a variant such as «لَتُهْدَى» is presumably meant]. In the codex (ḥarf) of Ubayy: وَإِنَّكَ لَتَدْعُوهُمْ إِلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ.

nahhas-irab:53-53.t: (صِراطِ اللَّهِ) [is genitive] as a badal (substitute). Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: the nominative and the accusative are also permissible. (أَلا إِلَى اللَّهِ تَصِيرُ الْأُمُورُ): and they always [go] to Him, the Exalted. Al-Akhfash said: Allah takes charge of affairs on the Day of Resurrection to the exclusion of His creation, whereas in this world some of them were in the hands of His creation, among the jurists, the rulers and others.

nahhas-irab:1-4.t: حم عسق كَذلِكَ يُوحِي إِلَيْكَ وَإِلَى الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ اللَّهُ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ: the kāf of «كذلك» is in the position of the accusative (naṣb), a naʿt (adjective) of a maṣdar (verbal noun); and the name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is nominative by «يوحي». The soundest thing said about the meaning is that it is: "like Our revealing to you and to those before you, it is revealed to you". Abū ʿUbayda permits «ذلك» to be taken in the sense of «هذا» ("this"). Whoever reads «يُوحَى إليك» (passive) [Translator's note: the passive reading is not distinguishable in the text as printed, which repeats يُوحِي إِلَيْكَ; it is supplied from the sense of the discussion] makes the kāf in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with the clause as the khabar (predicate), and the deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil) is latent (mustatir) in «يوحى»; and the name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, or by an implied verb, that is: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, reveals it to you. Whoever reads «نوحي» with nūn makes the name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with «العزيز الحكيم» as its khabar; and it is also possible that «العزيز الحكيم» is a naʿt, and the khabar is لَهُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: تَكادُ السَّماواتُ يَتَفَطَّرْنَ مِنْ فَوْقِهِنَّ: the soundest thing said about it is that the meaning is "from their upper parts"; and it is said: from above the earths. And I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: the pronoun refers to the disbelievers, that is, they would burst asunder from above the disbelievers because of their disbelief. Abū Jaʿfar said: we know of no grammarian who permitted «رأيتهنّ» ("I saw them", feminine plural) for human beings unless it is specifically for females. This indicates the unsoundness of this view; and moreover, there has been no previous mention of the disbelievers so that they could be alluded to. وَالْمَلائِكَةُ يُسَبِّحُونَ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّهِمْ وَيَسْتَغْفِرُونَ لِمَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ: something specific is meant by it, while its wording is general, that is, for the believers; and what indicates it is إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: وَالَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِهِ أَوْلِياءَ: nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); اللَّهُ حَفِيظٌ عَلَيْهِمْ: a mubtadaʾ and its khabar (predicate), in the position of the khabar of «الذين».

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: لِتُنْذِرَ أُمَّ الْقُرى وَمَنْ حَوْلَها: «من» is in the position of the accusative (naṣb), and the meaning is: that you may warn the people of the Mother of Cities and those around it. وَتُنْذِرَ يَوْمَ الْجَمْعِ: that is, the day on which people are gathered. لا رَيْبَ فِيهِ فَرِيقٌ: [فَرِيقٌ] is [nominative] as a mubtadaʾ (subject). Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ permitted the accusative of «فريق», with the meaning: "and that you may warn a party [who will be] in Paradise and a party in the Blaze on the Day of Gathering".

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: وَلَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ لَجَعَلَهُمْ أُمَّةً واحِدَةً: that is, believers. It is said: the meaning is: if Allah had willed, He would have compelled them to faith, and then there would have been no reward for them in it; so He tested them by removing compulsion from them. وَلكِنْ يُدْخِلُ مَنْ يَشاءُ فِي رَحْمَتِهِ — and they are the believers. وَالظَّالِمُونَ is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); and in another place [it is] وَالظَّالِمِينَ أَعَدَّ لَهُمْ عَذاباً أَلِيماً [al-Insān: 31]. The difference between them is that that one is followed by «أعدّ», whereas there is no verb after this one; that is, since a verb was implied for that one: "and He threatened the wrongdoers". [Translator's note: the text reads «وواعد», apparently for «وأوعد» ("and He threatened").]

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: فَاللَّهُ هُوَ الْوَلِيُّ: هُوَ may be redundant (zāʾida), with no grammatical position; and it may be a noun, nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with الْوَلِيُّ as its khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: وَمَا اخْتَلَفْتُمْ فِيهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ فَحُكْمُهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ: that is, it is referred back to Allah, either by an explicit text (naṣṣ) or by an indication (dalīl).

nahhas-irab:11-11.t:
فاطِرُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ: it may be nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), and it may be a naʿt (adjective). Al-Kisāʾī said:
فاطِرُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ in the accusative [i.e. «فاطرَ»; the vowel is printed as ḍamma in the text] is permissible, as a vocative (nidāʾ); and others said: as praise (madḥ). The genitive is also permissible, as a badal (substitute) from the hāʾ in «عليه». يَذْرَؤُكُمْ فِيهِ: Shuʿba said from Manṣūr: «يذرؤكم» means "He creates you". Abū Isḥāq said: «يذرؤكم» means "He multiplies you", and he took «فيه» in the sense of «به» ("by it"), that is, He multiplies you by making you pairs. ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: «يذرؤكم» means "He makes you grow from state to state", that is, He makes you grow in the making [of pairs]. Abū Jaʿfar said: the most correct of these views is what Shuʿba reported from Manṣūr, because the early philologists, among them Abū Zayd and others, reported from the Arabs: «ذرأ الله عزّ وجلّ الخلق يذرؤهم», that is, He created them. The view of Abū Isḥāq and Abū al-Ḥasan is figurative, and the literal meaning is more fitting, especially given the eminence of the one who held it, and since it is well known in the language. And taking «في» in its proper sense is more fitting than making it mean «به», even though one says «فلان بمكة» ("so-and-so is in Mecca"). So the meaning is: Allah has made for you from yourselves mates, creating you in [the state of being] pairs; and it is masculine according to the meaning of the plural. And the implied form is: and He has made for you of the livestock pairs, that is, males and females. لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ: that is, no one other than Him is able to do this. The kāf in كَمِثْلِهِ is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis (tawkīd), with no grammatical position because it is a particle, but the position of كَمِثْلِهِ is that of the accusative. The implied form is: «ليس مثله شيء» ("there is nothing like Him"). وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: لَهُ مَقالِيدُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa said from Ibn ʿAbbās: لَهُ مَقالِيدُ — he says: keys. إِنَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ: [عَلِيمٌ] is the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ», and the implied order is: «إنه عليم بكلّ شيء» ("He is Knowing of all things").

nahhas-irab:13-13.t:
شَرَعَ لَكُمْ مِنَ الدِّينِ ما وَصَّى بِهِ نُوحاً: «ما» is in the position of the accusative (naṣb) by «شرع». وَالَّذِي أَوْحَيْنا إِلَيْكَ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it. وَما وَصَّيْنا is also in the position of the accusative, that is, "and He ordained for you". وَما وَصَّيْنا بِهِ إِبْراهِيمَ وَمُوسى وَعِيسى أَنْ أَقِيمُوا الدِّينَ وَلا تَتَفَرَّقُوا فِيهِ: «أن» is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) from «ما», that is, He ordained for you: "Establish the religion". It may be in the position of the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), that is, "it is: establish the religion"; and it may be in the position of the genitive as a badal from the hāʾ, that is, He ordained for you that you establish for Allah the religion that He has approved, and that you not divide, believing in some of the messengers and disbelieving in others. So this is what He ordained for you, for all the prophets, may the blessings of Allah be upon them: that they establish the religion that He approved, which is Islam; and the community of Muḥammad ﷺ follows their example. In the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ: «Follow the example of those after me: Abū Bakr and ʿUmar», that is, act as they act in following the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and in leaving what goes against what they were commanded; its meaning is not [following them] in every question. أَنْ أَقِيمُوا الدِّينَ: it is permissible for «أقيموا», which is an imperative, to enter into the ṣila (relative clause), because its meaning is like the meaning of the imperfect verb; its meaning is: that you establish the religion and not divide in it. The position of a group of the exegetes is that Noah ﷺ was the first to bring the sacred law (sharīʿa), with the prohibition of [marrying] mothers, daughters, sisters and paternal aunts; and this view is included in the meaning of the first. كَبُرَ عَلَى الْمُشْرِكِينَ ما تَدْعُوهُمْ إِلَيْهِ: that is, establishing the religion for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, alone.
اللَّهُ يَجْتَبِي إِلَيْهِ مَنْ يَشاءُ: that is, whom He wills to choose; then this was omitted. وَيَهْدِي إِلَيْهِ مَنْ يُنِيبُ: the ḍamma was dropped from «يهدي» because of its heaviness; and «أناب» means "he returned", that is, he repented.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: وَما تَفَرَّقُوا إِلَّا مِنْ بَعْدِ ما جاءَهُمُ الْعِلْمُ: that is, after the Qurʾān came to them. بَغْياً is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and it is in reality a maṣdar (verbal noun).

nahhas-irab:15-15.t:
فَلِذلِكَ فَادْعُ وَاسْتَقِمْ كَما أُمِرْتَ: al-Farrāʾ holds that the meaning of the lām is the meaning of «إلى» ("to"), and that the meaning of «ذلك» is «هذا» ("this"), that is: so to this call, that is, to your establishing the religion and not dividing in it.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the lām in the sense of «إلى» is like His saying, Mighty and Majestic: بِأَنَّ رَبَّكَ أَوْحى لَها [al-Zalzala: 5]. Al-ʿAjjāj said: [al-Rajaz] 398-
وحى لها القرار فاستقرّت
("He inspired it to settle, and it settled.")
Abū Jaʿfar said: it is figurative, and al-Farrāʾ has been opposed on it; and it is said: the lām is in its proper sense.
The meaning is: because of what has been revealed to you — establishing the religion and abandoning division in it — for the sake of that, call. As for «ذلك» meaning «هذا», that is not permissible according to the skilled grammarians. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: «هذا» is for what is present and «ذلك» for what is distant, so letting one enter upon the other would be the nullification of clarity. «ذلك» is in its proper sense, that is: so to that which has preceded, call. وَلا تَتَّبِعْ أَهْواءَهُمْ: [أهواء] is the plural of «هوى», built on [the pattern] faʿal, except that it is weak, because the yāʾ was changed into an alif on account of its having a vowel and the letter before it having a vowel; so it was pluralised according to its original form, just as one says:
«جمل» and «أجمال». لا حُجَّةَ بَيْنَنا وَبَيْنَكُمُ: [حُجَّةَ] is accusative by the [lā of] absolute negation (tabriʾa, i.e. the lā of generic negation); we have already mentioned the reason for it. Sībawayh permitted the nominative, making «لا» mean «ليس». The meaning is that the truth has become clear and you are obstinate, and argument only holds against one who is not like that.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: وَالَّذِينَ is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); وحُجَّتُهُمْ is a second mubtadaʾ; داحِضَةٌ is the khabar (predicate) of «حجتهم», and the clause is the khabar of «الذين». It is also possible that «حجّتهم» is a badal (substitute) from «الذين», as a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl). There are two views on the meaning. One of them is that the meaning is: those who dispute concerning Allah after [the Prophet ﷺ] has been answered — so the hāʾ alludes to the Prophet ﷺ — that is, after he invoked [Allah] against the people of Badr and was answered, invoked drought against the people of Mecca and Muḍar and was answered, and prayed for the oppressed that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would rescue them from Quraysh and was answered, in other things besides these. [Translator's note: the text reads «ومصر» (Egypt); the well-known report concerns «مضر» (Muḍar).] The other view is that of Mujāhid; he said: those who dispute concerning Allah after He has been answered are a group of disbelievers who argue with the believers about Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that is, about His Oneness, after the believers have responded to Him; they argue while persisting in disbelief, waiting for the [days of] Ignorance (jāhiliyya) to come [back]. This view is more correct than the one before it and more consistent with the sequence of the verse, because there has been no previous mention of the Prophet ﷺ, nor of his invocation, so that he could be alluded to.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: اللَّهُ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ الْكِتابَ: the name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and الَّذِي is its khabar (predicate), not a naʿt (adjective), because the khabar is indispensable whereas the naʿt can be dispensed with. أَنْزَلَ الْكِتابَ بِالْحَقِّ: that is, He mentioned in it what people are rightly obliged to do. وَالْمِيزانَ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «الكتاب», that is, and He sent down the Balance with the truth. وَما يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّ السَّاعَةَ قَرِيبٌ: a threat to them, because they disputed concerning Allah, Mighty and Majestic, after He had been answered. He said «قريب» [masculine] while «الساعة» is feminine, by way of relation (nasab); and it is said: to distinguish it from [nearness of] kinship. As for Abū Isḥāq, he says: because the femininity is not real. And the meaning is: perhaps the Resurrection is near; and he mentioned another aspect, saying: it may be "perhaps the coming of the Hour is near".

nahhas-irab:18-19.t:
يَسْتَعْجِلُ بِهَا الَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِها: that is like their saying: مَتى هذَا الْوَعْدُ [Yūnus:
48]. وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مُشْفِقُونَ مِنْها: and such is the description of the people of faith: they fear falling short, lest they be punished for it. أَلا إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يُمارُونَ فِي السَّاعَةِ لَفِي ضَلالٍ بَعِيدٍ: that is, in straying from the truth; it became "far" only because they disbelieved out of obstinacy and rejection of the truth; had their disbelief been out of ignorance, it would not have been far, because [the truth] was becoming clear to them and they were seeing the proofs.

nahhas-irab:20-21.t: مَنْ كانَ يُرِيدُ حَرْثَ الْآخِرَةِ نَزِدْ لَهُ فِي حَرْثِهِ: a condition and its requital (mujāzāh). Abū Jaʿfar said: we have already mentioned several views on its meaning, and we [now] mention what we have not mentioned. It is that the meaning is: whoever by his jihād desires the Hereafter and its reward, We give him that and increase him; and whoever by his raiding desires the spoils — which is the harvest of this world, by way of likeness — We give him of it, because the Prophet ﷺ did not withhold the spoils from the hypocrites. This is a clear view, except that it is specific. And a general view was stated by Ṭāwūs; he said: whoever's concern is this world, Allah places his poverty between his eyes, and he obtains of this world only what was written for him; and whoever desires the Hereafter, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, places his richness between his eyes and illuminates his heart, and gives him of this world what was written for him.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t:
تَرَى الظَّالِمِينَ مُشْفِقِينَ مِمَّا كَسَبُوا: الظَّالِمِينَ is accusative by «ترى», and مُشْفِقِينَ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the implied meaning is: [fearful] of the punishment for what they earned. He, Mighty and Majestic, said: وَهُوَ واقِعٌ بِهِمْ, that is, the punishment. وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ فِي رَوْضاتِ الْجَنَّاتِ
Mujāhid said: «الروضة» is a pleasant, beautiful place. One of the philologists related that it is only in an elevated place — [if it is elevated] it is finer and stronger, and if [its ground] is rough and not soft its fruit is finer and more delicious — as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: كَمَثَلِ جَنَّةٍ بِرَبْوَةٍ [al-Baqara: 265], that is, elevated. Al-Aʿshā said: [al-Basīṭ] 399-
ما روضة من رياض الحزن معشبة ... خضراء جاد عليها مسبل هطل
("No meadow of the rugged upland, grassy and green, on which a heavy, pouring cloud has rained generously, [is lovelier than she].")
So he described it as one of the meadows of «الحزن», and «الحزن» is the rugged part of the land; one also says «الحزم» with mīm — for the reason we mentioned. ذلِكَ هُوَ الْفَضْلُ الْكَبِيرُ: that is, that which was mentioned before for those who believed.
«ذلك» is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «هو» is a second mubtadaʾ; it may also be redundant (zāʾida), for emphasis (tawkīd); «الفضل» is the khabar (predicate), and «الكبير» is its naʿt (adjective).

nahhas-irab:23-23.t:
ذلِكَ الَّذِي يُبَشِّرُ اللَّهُ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). The reading of the Kufans is يُبَشِّرُ [Translator's note: the variant is not distinguishable in the text as printed; the Kufan reading meant is «يَبْشُرُ»], and we have already mentioned its like; except that Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ read this one alone as يُبَشِّرُ [i.e. «يَبْشُرُ»] and read the others as «يبشّر». Some people objected to this in him, saying: there is no difference between this one and the others. The argument for him in that is that he did not read anything anomalous or far-fetched in Arabic; but since they are two eloquent dialects, he did not confine himself to one of them, lest the hearer imagine that nothing else is permissible, so he brought both of them. That is what the skilled do. And in the Qurʾān there is a parallel to it on which there is agreement, namely His saying, Mighty and Majestic: فَلْيُمْلِلْ وَلِيُّهُ بِالْعَدْلِ [al-Baqara: 282], from «أملّ يملّ», and in another place فَهِيَ تُمْلى عَلَيْهِ بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلًا [al-Furqān: 5], from «أملى يملي». قُلْ لا أَسْئَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ أَجْراً إِلَّا الْمَوَدَّةَ فِي الْقُرْبى: Abū Jaʿfar said: we have already mentioned its meaning exhaustively.
As for the iʿrāb, this is the place to mention it: «المودّة» is in the position of the accusative because it is an exception from what is not of the first [kind] (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ); Sībawayh represents it with the meaning of «لكن» ("but"), and so said Abū Isḥāq. He said: «أجرا» completes the speech, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: قُلْ ما أَسْئَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ [al-Furqān: 57]. Were it not an exception from what is not of the first kind, «المودة» would be a badal (substitute) from «أجر». وَمَنْ يَقْتَرِفْ حَسَنَةً: a condition; one says «اقترف» and «قرف» when one earns; and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is نَزِدْ لَهُ فِيها حُسْناً.

nahhas-irab:24-25.t:
The scholars differed on the interpretation of this. Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning of يَخْتِمْ عَلى قَلْبِكَ is: He will bind your heart with patience in bearing their harm. Abū Jaʿfar said: what he said does not resemble the apparent sense of the verse.
Others said: if Allah willed, He would seal your heart if you were to commit [such a thing]. And they differed on the meaning of يَخْتِمْ: some of them said: that is, He would prevent you from discernment. And some of them said: the meaning of "Allah sealed his heart" is: He placed on it a mark of blackness or something else by which the angels know that he is being punished, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: كَلَّا بَلْ رانَ عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ [al-Muṭaffifīn: 14]. Abū Jaʿfar said: in the exegesis [it is reported] that when a servant commits a sin, a stain (rayn) is placed on his heart and part of it is covered; if he increases, the stain is increased until his heart becomes black, and then he does not benefit from any admonition. وَيَمْحُ اللَّهُ الْباطِلَ is cut off from what precedes, in the position of the nominative. It ought to be written with wāw, except that it occurred in the written text (al-sawād) without wāw, written according to the pronunciation in continuous speech (idrāj); the wāw was dropped in continuous speech only because of its quiescence and the quiescence of the lām after it, so when you pause, the reason for its omission disappears. On this basis one should not pause on it, because if one keeps the wāw he contradicts the written text, and if he drops it he commits a solecism (laḥn). Its parallel is وَيَدْعُ الْإِنْسانُ بِالشَّرِّ [al-Isrāʾ: 11], and likewise سَنَدْعُ الزَّبانِيَةَ [al-ʿAlaq: 18]. As for the meaning of «ويمح الله الباطل», in it there is an argument against them for the prophethood of Muḥammad ﷺ, because its meaning is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, removes falsehood and does not establish it; so if what Muḥammad ﷺ brought were false, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would have effaced it and sent down a book to someone else. This has been the established pattern with all fabricators: that Allah, Glorified is He, effaces their falsehood with the truth, proofs and arguments. وَيُحِقُّ الْحَقَّ بِكَلِماتِهِ: that is, He makes the truth clear.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t:
It is possible that الَّذِينَ is in the position of the nominative by their [own] verb, that is: and those who believe respond to their Lord in what He called them to. It is also possible that «الذين» is in the position of the accusative, that is: and Allah responds to those who believe; and dropping the lām in this is permissible and frequent; its like is وَإِذا كالُوهُمْ [al-Muṭaffifīn: 3], that is, «كالوا لهم» ("measured for them").
Abū Jaʿfar said: this is more consistent with the sequence of the discourse, because the verb before it and the one after it belong to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. And there is a ḥadīth from Muʿādh ibn Jabal indicating this; he said: you pray for these craftsmen, "May Allah forgive you, have mercy on you and bless you," and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: وَيَسْتَجِيبُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ وَيَزِيدُهُمْ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ. On this basis «يزيدهم» means [He gives them more] than what they prayed for, and the statement is complete. وَالْكافِرُونَ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause is its khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:27-29.t: وَلَوْ بَسَطَ اللَّهُ الرِّزْقَ لِعِبادِهِ لَبَغَوْا فِي الْأَرْضِ: al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him, permitted that a sīn followed by a ṭāʾ be changed into a ṣād [i.e. «بصط»], because of its closeness to it. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that in His saying, Mighty and Majestic: وَمِنْ آياتِهِ خَلْقُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَما بَثَّ فِيهِما مِنْ دابَّةٍ, He, Mighty and Majestic, meant "and what He dispersed in the earth", not the heaven, and that its like is يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمَا اللُّؤْلُؤُ وَالْمَرْجانُ [al-Raḥmān: 22], whereas they come out only from the salt [sea]; and he claimed that this is how it came in the exegesis. Abū Jaʿfar said: what he said is not known in exegesis, nor in the language, nor in reason — that is, reporting about two things with one report [that applies to only one]; this is the nullification of clarity and a transgression into what religion forbids. The Arabs say of everything that moves: «دبّ», so it is «دابّ»; then they add the hāʾ for intensification and say «دابّة». Abū Jaʿfar said: and I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: [the hāʾ] in «دابّة» is for the feminine gender of the form.

nahhas-irab:30-30.t:
وَما أَصابَكُمْ مِنْ مُصِيبَةٍ فَبِما كَسَبَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ: this is the reading of the Kufans and the Basrans, and so it is in their codices; and the Medinans read «بما» without fāʾ, and so it is in their codices. The reading with the fāʾ is clear, because it is a condition and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). Concerning the reading without fāʾ the grammarians have three views. One of them: «ما» has the meaning of «الذي» ("that which"), so it needs no answer with the fāʾ; and this is the position of Abū Isḥāq. The second view:
«ما» is conditional and the fāʾ is omitted, as [the poet] said: [al-Basīṭ] 400
- من يفعل الحسنات الله يشكرها ... والشّرّ بالشّرّ عند الله مثلان
("Whoever does good deeds, Allah will thank him for them; and evil for evil, with Allah, are two equals.")
This is the view of Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān al-Akhfash, and he claimed that this indicates that dropping the fāʾ in a condition is permissible and good, because of the eminence of those who read it so. The third view: «ما» here is conditional, except that dropping the fāʾ is permissible because it does not govern anything in the wording, and it only falls on a past verb; and this is the most correct of the views. As for «ما» having the meaning of «الذي», that is far-fetched, because it would then be restricted to the past; and as for likening this to the verse we mentioned, that too is far-fetched, because dropping the fāʾ with an imperfect verb is not permissible according to Sībawayh except under poetic necessity, and the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is construed only according to what is most common and best known.
